title: Microglia: from surveillance to reactive
objective: Describe how microglia shift from surveillance to reactive states and why context matters.

steps.title: Never truly at rest
steps.body: Even 'resting' **[[microglia]]** constantly extend and retract processes, surveying the tissue. On sensing damage or infection they shift to **reactive** states — changing shape, migrating, releasing signals. The shift isn't simply on/off; it's context-dependent and can help or harm.

options: Continuously extending and retracting processes to survey the tissue
Sitting completely still and motionless until an injury happens to occur
Waiting in the bloodstream until an injury recruits them into the brain
Conducting their own action potentials, the same way neurons do
steps.explanation: In vivo imaging shows resting microglia are highly dynamic surveillants — 'resting' means not reactive, it doesn't mean motionless.

variants.setup: Two-photon imaging watches 'resting' microglia in a live brain.
variants.reveal: Resting microglia are dynamic surveillants, their processes always probing.

steps.setup: A paper labels microglia simply as 'activated = bad'.
steps.prompt: What's the problem with that framing?
options: Reactive states are context-dependent and can be protective or harmful
Microglia are never involved in protection, and only ever cause damage
Microglia cannot change their state at all once they have matured
Activation always repairs tissue perfectly and never causes any harm
steps.reveal: Reactive microglia can clear debris and contain damage or can drive injury, depending on context. A flat 'activated = bad' misses that — the field now describes states more carefully.

flag.note: Microglial 'states' are an active area; simple activated/resting or M1/M2 labels are increasingly seen as oversimplified.

variants.prompt: 'Activated microglia = bad' is a poor framing because…
options: Reactive states can be protective or harmful by context
Microglia only ever cause damage, never anything useful
Microglia can't change their state once they are mature
variants.explanation: Reactivity is context-dependent, not uniformly harmful.

flag.note: Microglial state labels are debated and increasingly seen as oversimplified.

sources.note: Resting microglia are highly dynamic surveillants of the brain in vivo.

reviewNotes: Microglial surveillance vs reactive; context-dependence flagged.
